synopsis: The University of Queensland’s ACARP C24028 project studied haul-truck proximity-advisory interface design in 2017, with follow-on work to 2019 [f3314, f15631]. It tested real operators in a machine simulator and used a 5DT haul-truck simulator to evaluate visual and auditory proximity interfaces aimed at reducing collision probability [f414, f572]. Its scope was advisory warnings and human–machine interfaces, not automatic braking, so it should not be treated as evidence of automatic-braking validation [f573, f13405]. The corpus uses this example when rating heavy-off-road operator-in-simulator testing maturity as Medium to High for human factors [f965]. Although the project chronology is given, the accessible project page does not state a clear publication date; Chapter 1 therefore describes the work as approximately 2017-era [f574, f3314].
